newsitem.title: USA: Draft Okla. City Schools audit hits D.A.'s office.
newsitem.headline: Draft Okla. City Schools audit hits D.A.'s office.

text.p: The head of the Oklahoma County District Attorney's white collar unit has reviewed a "preliminary draft audit" of the Oklahoma City Public School District, but said more work remains before a report can be released regarding alleged mishandling of district funds.

"There is nothing that is for release at this point in time, and I don't know exactly when it will be released," Phillip Stambeck, who heads the D.A.'s white collar unit, said. "This is just kind of the preliminary findings, and there is still quite a bit of work to be done by law enforcement before it can be released."
More work may be required from the state auditor's office, he said.

Stambeck said he requested the draft, which he received on Friday, following allegations of wrong doing involving the school district's activity funds, its self-insured workers compensation fund and some purchases.
"Anytime you get allegations of wrong doing of that magnitude, it needs an investigative audit," he said.
Cynthia Reid, director of communications for the Oklahoma City School District, said she had yet to see the draft.
"It's only gone to the D.A. and the (state) Attorney General, we still haven't seen a copy," she said. "We'd really like to see it before we make a comment."
